markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire when election results are certified.
markets.rules_primary: If the certified percentage of the popular vote received by Oliver Larkin in the 2026 FL-25 Democratic primary is 50% to 100%, inclusive of both endpoints, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary: The percentage is calculated as (total votes received by the specified person/party ÷ total valid votes cast) × 100, rounded to the specified decimal places. Resolution is based on certified/official results only, not preliminary results. Write-in votes are included if they appear in certified results. Invalid, spoiled, or rejected ballots are excluded from both numerator and denominator. If multiple rounds of voting occur (e.g., ranked choice voting), the percentage is based on the specified round or the first round if not specified. If the election is cancelled, postponed beyond the market expiration, or no certified results are available by expiration, the market resolves to No. If a recount changes the certified percentage before expiration, the most recent certified percentage is used.

Qualifying Release: The Payout Criterion is satisfied if OpenAI releases a model that either (a) is publicly named "Astra" (including numbered, lettered, or suffixed variants such as "Astra 1," "Astra 6," or "GPT-6 Astra"), or (b) is confirmed by OpenAI, or by a consensus of credible reporting, to share the same underlying model — including the same base architecture, weights, or training run — as the model referenced in OpenAI's August 1, 2026 disclosure, regardless of the commercial name, safety configuration, or access tier under which it is ultimately released. A separately-branded release that is derived from or built on the same underlying model as the disclosed Astra model satisfies this clause even if OpenAI markets it as a distinct product (e.g., a safety-restricted variant or a differently-priced tier), provided the shared underlying model is confirmed by OpenAI or by a consensus of credible reporting.

markets.rules_primary: If United States of America v. James Brien Comey, Jr. has been dismissed by the court or administrative body with jurisdiction after Issuance and before Jan 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
A dismissal is defined as:

For Criminal Cases:
Dismissal of charges by prosecutor (nolle prosequi)
Court-ordered dismissal for constitutional violations
Dismissal for speedy trial violations
Dismissal for prosecutorial misconduct
Dismissal for insufficient evidence
Dismissal following successful motion to dismiss

The following do NOT constitute dismissals:
Settlement agreements between parties
Plea bargains or guilty pleas in criminal cases
Default judgments
Summary judgments on the merits
Trial verdicts (guilty, not guilty, liable, not liable)
Consent decrees or agreed orders
Cases transferred to different courts
Cases stayed or continued indefinitely
Bankruptcy discharge (which is a substantive resolution)
Cases resolved through alternative dispute resolution
Appeals or remands (unless the appellate court dismisses the case entirely)
Temporary restraining orders or preliminary injunctions
Administrative closure

If only some claims, counts, or defendants are dismissed while the case continues on other matters, this does NOT constitute a dismissal for purposes of this contract. The entire case must be dismissed.

A full solo performance of one or more songs.

A performance that begins within the official event timeframe but extends beyond it due to scheduling overrun, provided the performance commenced during the official timeframe.

A performance at a rescheduled version of Lollapalooza Chicago 2027 where the reschedule occurs within one year of the original event date, pursuant to the postponement provisions below.

A performance that begins within the official event timeframe but extends beyond it due to scheduling overrun, provided the performance commenced during the official timeframe.

A performance at a rescheduled version of Lollapalooza Chicago 2027 where the reschedule occurs within one year of the original event date, pursuant to the postponement provisions below.
